contracts: Each test asserts rd_vm::PORTABLE_CORE and executes real DEX on the original portable Engine; worker identities/delivery and EGL provider are controlled host adapters, not OS scheduling/GPU evidence.

Initial default is null. Per-thread handler wins over the root delegation group; clearing restores group fallback. Thread exit clears handler; a later explicit handler follows API26 getter/setter semantics.

Automatic delivery invokes a real virtual getUncaughtExceptionHandler override, then the actual handler uncaughtException(Thread,Throwable) on the throwing worker before active/callback owner scope exits.

The original Throwable and handler failure remain distinct. VM-built exceptions use Engine materialization; an OOM/lookup/materialization/handler failure never replaces the original returned Java exception.

Root tickets preserve original local-only Throwable during GC inside an overridden getter, retain handler/Thread objects through mutation, GC and nested native-to-DEX reentry, and keep reports alive after guest static roots are removed.

Default and per-thread handlers survive GC without guest static references. Direct root ThreadGroup delegation invokes the actual default. A wrong-type setter throws ClassCastException and preserves the prior handler.
Caught Java exceptions and structured non-Java VmExit errors do not trigger handlers. Main lifecycle escape is delivered once; worker errors forwarded through the main pump are not delivered again.
Timer and GLSurface queue exception tests observe actual modeled throwing-owner Thread identity, original Throwable identity, and isAlive=true during the handler.
Latest128 diagnostic reports are retained. Main exception scopes use exact unique RAII tickets and no service RefCell borrow is held across DEX/native calls.
